prompt.context: Our client, Brandy Thomas-Chase (BTC), is a high-powered Black financial player and owns one of the most successful VC firms in the country. She has come to us with an issue near and dear to her heart. She believes that mid to large-sized banks have ignored an important potential consumer segment: the underbanked, usually found in underserved minority populations. BTC wants our thoughts on how she can leverage her firm to remedy this injustice, as well as how big this opportunity could be.
prompt.question: How should BTC leverage her VC firm to increase banking access for underbanked populations, and how large is this opportunity?

clarifying_info.q: Is the client currently in the banking space?
clarifying_info.a: No, the client is not currently in the banking space directly.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a return threshold or expected timeline to recoup the investment?
clarifying_info.a: No, the client does not have a threshold or an expected timeline in mind.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's primary objective?
clarifying_info.a: The main objective is to increase access of some form of banking to underbanked populations.

clarifying_info.q: Would the client consider building something from scratch?
clarifying_info.a: Though they typically invest in somewhat established organizations, the client is interested in what taking on this project from the start would look like.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have the capital to take this on?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, assume they will have the capital ready.
An underbanked household is one that has a bank account, but goes outside of the bank for financial services such as money orders, cashing, payday loans, etc.

framework: Attractiveness — Market Size: How many underbanked households exist? Expected value per customer? Demographic makeup (age, regions)?

Attractiveness — Financials: Revenue streams (loans, fees, advertising); initial investment costs (brick-and-mortar buildout or digital development); ongoing fixed costs (rent, PPE) and variable costs (marketing, personnel)
Feasibility — Company and Competition: Too far from core competencies? Brand impact; CSR signal; incumbents and their success; competitive positioning
Feasibility — Mode of Entry: Organic (internal capabilities and capital); Partner/JV (work with existing banks near underserved areas, non-traditional partnerships with Venmo or grocery stores)
Other — Opportunity Cost: Is there a more attractive opportunity? Alternative ways to help the group, e.g., funding financial literacy programs?

questions.prompt: How would you think through arriving at the number of underbanked households in the country?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a top-down market sizing. Strong answers note that underbanked households still have a bank account so the rate is under 50%. Connecting to the U.S. poverty rate (~12-13%) as a reference point before being told the actual figure (15%) is a sign of strong reasoning.

math.setup: Start from U.S. population, convert to households, apply underbanked rate.
steps: Step 3: Number of households = 320M / 3 = ~100 million households (or 320M / 2.5 = ~128M; ~100M is the working assumption)
Step 4: Underbanked rate = 15% (tell the candidate if they do not arrive here themselves)
Step 5: Underbanked households = 100M x 15% = 15 million households (total addressable market)
math.answer: ~15 million underbanked households in the United States

questions.prompt: Many underbanked individuals lack access to brick-and-mortar banks. What are some ways BTC can fix this, and what should be considered with each option?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate multiple entry modes with balanced pros and cons. The recommended path is a neobank (digital-only). Strong candidates also weigh cost, control, reach, and regulatory hurdles for each option.

questions.prompt: How much will it cost to take on this endeavor and what is the NPV?
questions.guidance: Candidate should walk through upfront investment, annual costs (personnel + fixed/regulatory), annual revenue from customers, derive annual profit, apply perpetuity discount, then subtract upfront investment to get NPV.

math.setup: NPV = (Annual Profit / Discount Rate) - Upfront Investment. Annual Profit = Total Yearly Revenue - Total Yearly Costs. Total Yearly Costs = Personnel Costs + Fixed/Regulatory Costs.
steps: Customers: Digital bank serves 10% of 15M underbanked households = 1.5 million households
Revenue per customer: $1/month in user fees = $12/year per household
Personnel: 20 engineers + 80 digital bankers = 100 staff at $130K/yr = $13M/year
Fixed/Regulatory Costs: Servers/Licensing/Other Tech Fees $1M + Regulatory (quarterly payments of $125K = $500K/yr) + General Operating Expenses $500K = $2M/year

brainstorming.prompt: Many underbanked individuals lack access to brick-and-mortar banks. What are some ways that we can fix this? What should be considered with each?

categories.name: Joint Venture with Big Bank
ideas: Pro: Leverage brand name, expertise, and infrastructure of big bank
Con: Some level of control is lost
Con: Big banks have not played in this space; may need to prove value
Con: Lack of trust in large institutions among underbanked communities

categories.name: Build Brick and Mortar (Organic)
ideas: Pro: Full control over operations and profits
Pro: Able to control branding and image
Pro: Can leverage the building for other services (e.g., Starbucks on ground floor)
Con: Expensive — likely the most costly option
Con: Government regulations and permits could delay buildout
Con: No experience building in poor/underserved areas

categories.name: NeoBank (Digital-Only Bank) — Recommended
ideas: Pro: Can reach the largest number of people
Pro: More companies able to advertise on digital platform (more revenue)
Con: Limited services — e.g., mortgage agreements cannot be made digitally
Con: Lack of internet access in some underserved areas
Con: Uncomfortable for older, non-digital-native populations

recommendation: BTC should move forward with the neobank investment. Although the NPV is relatively low at $500K, this endeavor will help close the gap on racial inequity and position BTC to identify other opportunities to engage with this group, whether by creating additional financial products or otherwise. It will also allow BTC to expand its digital capabilities.
risks: Costs may be understated and revenues overstated
Regulations within the banking industry are very stringent and can delay project start, especially as they relate to online/digital banking
Unable to reach the target population and gain their trust
next_steps: Further validate cost and revenue assumptions
Engage with policy experts to understand regulatory procedures in this space
Think through strategic marketing efforts and tactics to reach end users in underbanked communities
